name: post-copy
summary: Brand-neutral rules for social post copy written from a video: read the transcript, promise only what is on screen, search words first on search platforms and hook first on browse platforms, 3 options from 3 angle families, few relevant hashtags, links where each platform tolerates them, plain specific sentences with no marketing filler. Brand voice, product facts, names and links come from /publish/knowledge/README.md, which wins over this file on voice. The honesty rules and hard platform limits here always win.

rules: The knowledge README sets the voice: person, tone, banned words, punctuation and spelling. These defaults apply where it is silent, and voice.banned is only a starting list.
Every option carries at least one concrete detail from the transcript: a step, a screen, a part, a version or a number.
Plain verbs. Contractions are fine. Digits for numbers. At most one exclamation mark per option.
At most one intensifier per option. ALL CAPS only for one word in a hype-tone YouTube title.
Emoji never replace words. No emoji walls. Counts follow params.emoji.
At most one of the three options per platform opens with a question.
No 'easy', 'fast', 'in X minutes' or 'free' unless the transcript and runtime prove it.
Never fake typos, fake anecdotes or fake urgency to sound human.

State the fact or the moment instead of staging it: no 'it's not X, it's Y', no question answered in the next line, no three fragments in a row for rhythm, no last line that repeats the post as a moral.

principles.title: Promise only what is on screen
principles.rule: Every claim, number, version, time and feature in the copy must appear in the video. Build a fact list from the transcript first and write only from it.
principles.why: YouTube A/B tests pick winners on watch time share, not CTR, and misleading metadata breaks spam policy. A mismatch loses the viewer after the click.

principles.title: Title and thumbnail are one unit
principles.rule: Look at the chosen thumbnail before writing a title. The title adds what the thumbnail does not say; never repeat the thumbnail text verbatim.
principles.why: Viewers read both together. Only 6.3% of breakout videos repeat the title on the thumbnail.

principles.title: Lead with the words people search
principles.rule: Pick 1 to 2 main search words (for example 'replace disc brake pads') and place them in the title and the first line of every description and caption.
principles.why: YouTube says to feature 1 to 2 main words in title and description. TikTok reads captions, voiceover and on-screen text. LinkedIn's feed model reads what a post is about.

principles.title: Front-load YouTube titles
principles.rule: Subject, keyword and payoff inside the first ~50 characters. Total length usually 40 to 70, never over 100.
principles.why: Truncation length is not official, so protect the first ~50 chars. 30 to 50 chars did best overall (vendor, correlational); how-to titles had a median of 55 chars.

principles.title: Specific beats clever
principles.rule: Name the real thing: the product, the screen, the step, the version. Prefer a specific frame over a generic formula or adjective.
principles.why: In 4M+ 2026 uploads, specific story frames beat generic formulas; plain how-to averaged 1.07x.

principles.title: Brand voice from knowledge, plain defaults otherwise
principles.rule: Apply the voice set in /publish/knowledge/README.md to every option, field and platform. Where it is silent, apply voice.rules and voice.banned. Knowledge wins over this file on voice; the honesty rules and hard platform limits win over knowledge.
principles.why: Only the brand can say how it sounds. Without that, plain specific copy is the safe default, because hype and filler read as ads.

principles.title: Run the rewrite pass the knowledge names
principles.rule: If /publish/knowledge/README.md names a rewrite or style pass, run it on every title, text, firstComment and thread post, and on the prose in why and notes, before writing copy.json. Save the final text only, with no change list. The pass never adds a fact: fix a vague line with a fact from the fact list or cut it. Leave hashtags, tags, links, handles, product names, chapter lines and words quoted from the video as they are.
principles.why: The panel posts copy.json as is, so the pass has to be finished before the file is written.

principles.title: Few, relevant hashtags
principles.rule: Use the count in params.hashtags, capped by platforms.<key>.limits.hashtagsMax. Most specific first, at most one broad tag, never generic tags like #fyp, #viral, #reels or #explore. Never inline in text.
principles.why: TikTok says loosely related tags can work against you. Instagram caps at 5 and says hashtags do not raise reach. Meta limits reach for hashtag-heavy captions.

principles.title: Statements, not question titles
principles.rule: Do not end YouTube titles with a question. At most one question opener across the three options on any platform.
principles.why: Question-ending titles averaged 0.82x across 4M+ uploads (vendor, correlational).

principles.title: Use how-to wording for searched tasks
principles.rule: When the video teaches a task people search for (installing, fixing, setting up), one option should use plain how-to wording with the subject's full name.
principles.why: How-to titles had a median of 1.60x channel baseline vs 0.99x, credited to search intent. The ranked tutorials in the observed examples follow this pattern.

principles.title: Put links where the platform tolerates them
principles.rule: YouTube description and Bluesky body: links fine. Facebook, LinkedIn, Threads: link in firstComment. Instagram and TikTok: 'link in bio' or 'on our YouTube'. X: keep the post link-free and tell the user in notes to reply with the link.
principles.why: Non-Premium X link posts had 0% median engagement. Facebook warns links in captions may cut reach and tested link limits. Bluesky says it does not de-promote links.

principles.title: Fit caption length to the platform
principles.rule: TikTok: under 30 words by default, never over 90. Instagram Reels: 30 to 90 words. Facebook Reels: 30 to 60 words. LinkedIn text: 30+ words.
principles.why: TikTok under 30 words 4.90% vs 90+ 3.90%; Reels 30 to 90 words 0.25% vs 0.20%; Facebook Reels 30 to 60 words 0.28% vs 0.15% under 30; LinkedIn text under 30 words 2.40% vs about 3.7%.

principles.title: No engagement bait
principles.rule: Never ask for likes, shares, 'comment YES' or 'agree?'. A comment CTA is one real question tied to the video.
principles.why: LinkedIn filters engagement bait; Meta limits spammy captions.

principles.title: Match the spoken and on-screen words
principles.rule: Reuse the words the speaker says. For short-form, add a notes line asking for the keyword in on-screen text and voiceover.
principles.why: TikTok uses voiceover, captions and on-screen text to understand a video; many viewers watch muted.

principles.title: Chapters from the transcript
principles.rule: Long-form YouTube descriptions get chapters: 00:00 first, at least 3, ascending, each 10+ seconds, labels in plain words. Use placeholders and say so in notes if timings are unreliable.
principles.why: YouTube recommends chapters; manual chapters override automatic ones.

principles.title: Three options, three angle families
principles.rule: Exactly 3 options per platform, one from each angle family (search, browse, voice). Not three rewordings.
principles.why: format.md requires different angles; YouTube A/B tests need meaningfully different variants.

principles.title: YouTube tags for variants only
principles.rule: 5 to 10 tags: the main keyword, name variants and common misspellings. Each max 100 chars, total max 500.
principles.why: YouTube says tags play a minimal role and help mainly with misspellings.

principles.title: Version or year tag only when true
principles.rule: Add a version, month or year to tutorial titles only when it is on screen and current.
principles.why: Ranked tutorials in the observed examples carry a version or year because setups change (observed, one niche).

principles.title: Use the first comment for help, not hashtags
principles.rule: firstComment holds the main link or a real support prompt. Never the hashtag block.
principles.why: Replying to comments lifted engagement on every platform Buffer measured.

principles.title: Make origin clear
principles.rule: Write in the first person the knowledge README sets ('we' or 'I') and name the maker, so it is clear who made the footage and the thing shown.
principles.why: Meta and Instagram favor original content and reduce reach for reposts.

principles.title: Facts and links from knowledge or the video only
principles.rule: Links, handles, versions, prices, requirements and product facts come only from /publish/knowledge (and any skill it names) or the video, copied character for character. Use the deepest page that fits. Missing link: leave it out and say so in notes. Never a placeholder, never a guess. Nothing from the knowledge 'never claim' list.
principles.why: The panel posts copy.json as is, so a guessed URL or a placeholder goes out live.

principles.title: Open short-form on the moment
principles.rule: On short-form and feed posts, the first line names the one concrete moment the clip shows: who does what, and where. Feature lists, tooling and setup steps belong in tutorials.
principles.why: TikTok asks for a hook in the first seconds and says many viewers watch muted, so the first line and the on-screen text carry it (official). That a named moment beats a feature list is unverified: check it against your own analytics.

principles.title: The searched name, not only your own
principles.rule: Titles and first lines use the names and category words newcomers type, written in full (for example 'disc brake pads' next to the bike's model name). A project or product name alone is not what people who have never heard of it search for.
principles.why: Follows from featuring 1 to 2 main search words in the title and description (official). The size of the effect is unverified.

principles.title: Availability posts carry a number and one link
principles.rule: A launch, an opening, a restock, a deadline or a countdown: say it with a real number or time and one working link.
principles.why: Unverified, no public study behind it. People can only act on the post if it gives the time and the link.

principles.title: No templated captions
principles.rule: Never reuse the same date, version or 'Part x/y' line as the caption or title across posts. Each post names its own moment.
principles.why: YouTube asks for a unique description per video (official). The effect on short-form reach is unverified.

principles.title: One CTA, a link that resolves today
principles.rule: One CTA per post, placed where the platform allows a link (description, bio, pinned or first comment, X reply). Use the permanent links from knowledge, and list in notes every link the user should check before posting.
principles.why: Old posts keep getting views, so an expired invite or a moved page leaves the CTA pointing at a dead end (observed).

youtube.label: YouTube (long-form and Shorts)

hashtags.placement: Appended to the description by the panel. The first 3 show above the title. Never in the title.

structure: Title: subject + keyword + payoff in the first ~50 chars; statement, not a question.
Line 1: what the viewer gets, with the 1 to 2 search words.
Line 2: who made it, in one line, in the knowledge voice.
What you need (bullets when technical).
Chapters: 00:00 first, 3+, ascending, 10s+ each.
Links from knowledge or the video, deepest page that fits.
Shorts: short hook-first title, 1-line description, 2 hashtags.
youtube.cta: After line 2 of the description, never in line 1. Pinned firstComment carries the main link or a support prompt.
avoid: More than one ALL CAPS word
Time or 'easy' claims the video does not prove
unverified: Title truncation length (about 70 desktop search, 50 to 60 mobile, vendor only)

tiktok.label: TikTok

hashtags.placement: Appended after the caption by the panel. Specific first, at most one broad tag.

structure: Line 1: hook with the keyword in the first words.
Line 2: one concrete detail from the video.
Optional CTA: 'Full walkthrough on our YouTube' for tutorials; for clips, the bio link or the pinned comment. One CTA.
Default under 30 words; never over 90.
tiktok.cta: End of caption. Links are not clickable in captions, so point to YouTube or the bio.
avoid: Captions that describe things not in the clip
The same date or version line on every post
unverified: Hashtag cap of 5 (vendor and press reports, no TikTok statement)

instagram.label: Instagram Reels

hashtags.placement: Appended to the caption by the panel. Not in a comment: search reads captions.

structure: First ~125 chars: hook plus keyword.
1 to 3 short lines on what the Reel shows.
CTA line.
30 to 90 words.
instagram.cta: 'Full guide: link in bio' or 'on our YouTube'. Links are not clickable in captions or comments.
avoid: Hashtag block in the first comment
unverified: Cap of 5: announced Dec 2025 but the Graph API doc still says 30

facebook.label: Facebook (Reels and feed)

hashtags.placement: Appended by the panel. Never a block of tags.

structure: Reels: a title (same promise as the YouTube title, shorter) plus a 30 to 60 word caption.
Feed: 2 to 4 plain lines with the video uploaded natively.
Say who made it, in the first person, so the footage reads as original.
facebook.cta: Link in firstComment, never in the caption body.
unverified: Reels title limit of 255 (vendor API docs)

linkedin.label: LinkedIn

hashtags.placement: Appended at the end by the panel.

structure: Line 1 stands alone above the fold: what was built or shipped, named plainly.
2 to 4 short paragraphs: what the video shows, who it is for, one honest detail from making it.
Optional closing question that people in the field can answer.
linkedin.cta: Link in firstComment by default; a closing question only if it is real.
unverified: Fold at about 140 chars mobile and 210 desktop
Size of any link penalty (studies conflict)

twitter.label: X

hashtags.placement: Appended by the panel and counted in the 280.

structure: One or two sentences, fact first, video uploaded natively.
Long length: 3 to 5 posts in thread, each understandable alone.
No link in the post; notes tells the user to reply with it.
twitter.cta: In the post text ('video below'); the link goes in a reply the user posts, flagged in notes. X has no firstComment field.
unverified: X Help Center advice of max 2 hashtags (reported, not read)

threads.label: Threads

hashtags.placement: One topic tag, 1 to 50 chars, no periods or ampersands. Appended by the panel.

structure: Conversational, 1 to 3 short paragraphs.
End on something people can honestly answer.
thread only when length is long.
threads.cta: Link in firstComment; a real question at the end.

bluesky.label: Bluesky

hashtags.placement: Appended to the text by the panel and counted in the 300 graphemes. Keep the keyword in plain text too.

structure: One short post: what it is, what the video shows, link.
Long length: 3 to 5 posts in thread.
Plain or technical tone.
bluesky.cta: Link in the body is fine; keep the URL short.
unverified: hashtagsMax 8 is the out-of-text tags field; in-text hashtags have no separate cap beyond 300 graphemes

angles.name: Outcome
angles.when: Default search option: what the viewer has at the end, with the keyword.
angles.example: How to Replace Disc Brake Pads on a Fernhollow Trail 2

angles.name: Obstacle removed
angles.when: The video clearly solves a step people get stuck on. Name the step; only if the transcript shows the fix.
angles.example: New Brake Pads Too Tight: Push the Pistons Back First

angles.name: Time or effort
angles.when: Only when the runtime and transcript prove the time claim.
angles.example: Replace Disc Brake Pads in [proven minutes] Minutes

angles.name: Show it working
angles.when: The video has a strong visual moment: the finished result, the thing working, a before and after.
angles.example: Worn Brake Pads vs New, on the Same Hill

angles.name: Honest curiosity
angles.when: Browse feeds. Open a gap the video closes in the first seconds. No bait, no question title on YouTube.
angles.example: The 2 Tools You Need to Replace Disc Brake Pads

angles.name: From the makers
angles.when: Always one option. We made it; here is how to use it. Strongest on LinkedIn, X, Bluesky.
angles.example: We Build the Trail 2. Here's How We Change Its Brake Pads

angles.name: The moment
angles.when: Short-form and feeds, when the clip has one striking moment. Name the moment and the place first, then the subject and the search words.
angles.example: 20 hard stops down Mill Hill to bed in new disc brake pads

angles.name: Availability
angles.when: A launch, an opening, a restock, a deadline or a countdown. A real number or time and one working link.
angles.example: Trail 2 preorders open Friday at 9:00. 200 frames in the first batch.

angles.name: Candid update
angles.when: X, YouTube descriptions and progress updates, when the knowledge voice allows candor. What works now, a before and after number if there is one, plus one true limit. Never invent a flaw.
angles.example: We got [thing from the video] working. Still rough in [true limit from the video], fixing that next.

tone.plain: State what it is and what you get. Adjectives only when they carry a fact.
tone.hype: Energy from facts and verbs. Allows one ALL CAPS word in a YouTube title and one exclamation mark per option. No banned words, no claims beyond the video.
tone.dry-funny: One understated line per option about the subject or the work behind it. Never at the viewer's expense. Search words still lead on YouTube.
tone.technical: Name parts exactly as shown: versions, part numbers, settings, file names. Best for expert audiences on YouTube, LinkedIn, Bluesky.

long.youtube: full write-up up to about 2000 chars: requirements, steps, troubleshooting

cta.none: No ask. End on the last fact.
cta.watch: Point to the full video ('Full walkthrough on our YouTube'); on YouTube point to the next video or playlist.
cta.comment: One real question a viewer can answer from experience. Never 'comment YES' or 'agree?'.
cta.follow: A true reason to follow ('we post every repair guide here').
cta.link: The link from the request or from knowledge, placed per links-out-of-body.
cta.community: The brand's community (a Discord server, forum or newsletter) with a true reason, using the invite or link from knowledge. Never invent invites or channel names. Placement follows links-out-of-body.

params.keywords: Must-include search words. First keyword inside the first ~50 chars of the YouTube title and in the first line of every description and caption; mention it for on-screen text in notes. Once per title, once or twice per body. Variants go in YouTube tags. Never a keyword list.

light.rule: At a line end, never in a YouTube title, never replacing a word.

some.rule: Up to 3 on TikTok, Instagram, Threads; max 1 on YouTube, LinkedIn, X. X counts each emoji as 2 chars.

params.hashtags: Target count, capped by platforms.<key>.limits.hashtagsMax (Threads 1, Instagram 5, TikTok 5). 0 is valid. Specific first, at most one broad tag, no generic tags, never inline in text.
params.language: BCP-47 code. Write natively, do not translate idioms. Keep the proper names from knowledge unchanged. Use the local search words for the subject. For non-English Bluesky posts add a notes line to set the post language.

humanize.0: Clean neutral copy. Knowledge rules on banned words and punctuation still apply.
humanize.1: Plain voice: contractions, plain verbs, no hype.
humanize.2: Plus the first person from knowledge ('we' or 'I') and one maker's detail from the transcript.
humanize.3: Plus one honest aside (what was hard, what changed), uneven sentence lengths, fragments allowed. Never fake typos or stories.

params.audience: Free text from the panel. It sets the reader's vocabulary and what goes up front: beginners get the outcome and the steps, experts get exact names and how it works inside, buyers get the price and what they need, industry peers get what was built and why (LinkedIn first).
params.notes: User free text. Follow it unless it breaks a hard rule (honesty, platform limits, the knowledge 'never claim' list); then follow the rule and explain in that platform's notes.
